status: Prediction before expression decoder implementation and vendor probing
authority: DWARF 5 sections 2.5, 2.6 and 7.7/Table 7.9; named SDK Mach-O declarations for synthetic oracle inputs

gnu_probe_prediction.discovery: Enumerate vendor opcode bytes 0xe0 through 0xff in independently bounded expression attributes. Record complete oracle output, including errors; do not infer semantics from a vendor mnemonic.
gnu_probe_prediction.layout_controls: After the oracle identifies the two observed GNU operation names, probe known following opcodes, a one-byte nested expression, a multi-byte ULEB nested length and a truncated nested block. No numeric alias or operand layout enters the decoder before these observations.
gnu_probe_prediction.never_read: No unwinder, debugger, object-library or DWARF-library implementation source

census_text_measurement.qualification: Counts derive from the saved per-producer expression text; not a completed byte-decoder corpus census. Count nested operation tokens and entry_value/GNU_entry_value parentheses, not execution steps.

planned_caps.operation_headroom: 68.26 times the largest saved expression-token count
planned_caps.depth_headroom: 64 times the largest saved entry nesting
planned_caps.qualification: Operation and depth caps apply to one expression; caller supplies a remaining global work budget and receives the remainder. Full byte-corpus maxima remain to be checked before final lane acceptance.

representation: Flat pre-order records with absolute byte offsets, depth, parent index, subtree end, raw operand spans, signed and unsigned values, bounded branch targets and bounded DIE references. No expression execution or stack/process value inference.
deferred_validation: Actual DIE-start/type validation belongs to the DIE graph. addrx/constx operands remain indexes for the indexed-table reader to validate and resolve.
red_first: nested block bounds and parent markers
branch target bounds and instruction boundaries
